chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
A slave of Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib died, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) handed over his inheritance to the daughter of Hamza.

key_terms.حَمْزَةُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ: Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, uncle of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: Who inherits the estate of a freed slave according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the legal principle of 'wilayah al-muwalli' (guardianship of the emancipator), where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) assigned the inheritance of a freed slave to Hamza's daughter, reflecting the status of the mawla as part of the master's lineage. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a primary evidence for the mawla's right to inherit from their patron in the absence of other heirs, emphasizing the social and legal bonds created through manumission. The narration underscores the Prophet's direct application of this rule, reinforcing its authenticity and practical implementation in early Islamic society.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, from Safwan, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, from the one who narrated it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A slave of Hamza Bin Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup> died, so Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> handed over his inheritance to a daughter of Hamza’.
en.sarwar: 6. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad from Safwan from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from those who narrated to him who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

When a mawla of Hamzah ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib died, the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, gave his legacy to the daughter of Hamzah.’” Al-Hassan has said that this proves that the mawla did not have any daughter as al-‘A’ammah narrate, and that women also inherit guardianship contrary to what al-‘A’ammah narrate.
